artifact_purpose: R03 of plans/pe08_review_and_pe09_handoff_tickets.md. A deterministic comparison can be syntactically correct and still compare two different relationships. This record adjudicates every such dispute the R02 review raised: what the rule compared, what the copy and the sources actually say, what that means, and what is left for the operator. Each row separates a measurement from an interpretation and gives each its own status, so a reader can see where the evidence stops and the reading begins.
declared_by: drafted in a Claude Code session, 2026-10-07; every interpretation is a provisional reading for operator review and none records an operator decision
status_note: status is the status of the statement it sits on (CLAUDE.md 12.2): Confirmed where a named source evidences it directly, Inferred where it follows from confirmed evidence, Assumed where it rests on no direct evidence, Unresolved where this copy and these sources cannot settle it.
classification_note: classification uses the five the ticket names and two more. actual_inconsistency: the two things compared disagree and the candidate states both. ambiguous_relationship: the two things compared are different properties, or the comparison is sound and what it means is not settled by the sources available. extraction_issue: the text a check read is not the text the page carries. sanitisation_limitation: the evidence a claim needs was removed from this copy. unsupported_checker_assumption: a rule compares relations the sources do not tie, or expects a value no source requires. The two added: unsupported_lane_claim, a blind-lane statement the input that lane received contradicts - none of the five, because nothing was mis-extracted, nothing was removed and no deterministic rule is involved; and dispute_not_sustained, a dispute the review raised that the measurement does not sustain, where the row stands as recorded. No enum of any existing report is changed by this record.
failure_mode_note: failure_mode applies to a row the harness missed: evidence_not_read when no lane output engages with the point, evidence_read_and_rated_adequate when a lane cited the passage and judged it sufficient, evidence_read_and_misattributed when a lane credited one artifact with a neighbouring artifact's property, evidence_read_but_not_interrogated when a lane read the passage and asked a different question of it. The distinction is recorded, not counted: no rate in any artifact uses it.

adjudications.subject: the rule that a doctoral candidate's appointment must end inside the window of every work package the candidate's own project names
adjudications.rule: dc_table_vs_projects reported out_of_window when start + duration - 1 exceeded the end month of a work package named on the candidate's host line in 1.1.

compared_relation.left: the appointment period of the recruitment table: a planned start month plus a duration in months
compared_relation.right: the activity window of a work package: a start month and an end month

measured.statement: All nine appointments read M5 and 36 months, so each ends M40. All seven work packages run M1-M36. The rule therefore fired nine times, once per candidate, with the same arithmetic. The candidate states no project duration anywhere.

evidence.quote: | DC1 | Academic Beneficiary A | Academic Beneficiary A | M5 | 36 | 12 | 9 |
WP title: Impact and Innovation Start month – End month: M1 – M36

evidence.locator: Table 3.1d DC Table, the duration column header
evidence.quote: 3-36 (up to 48 for DN-JD)

evidence.locator: Table 3.1d DC Table, the start column header
evidence.quote: Planned Start Month

evidence.statement: A search of all three sections for a stated project duration returns nothing: the only occurrences of 48 are M7.3's due month and a training-day topic in 1.3 ('sustainability beyond project duration').

evidence.text: DC1 runs M5-M40 (36 months); WP1 ends M36, WP2 ends M36, WP4 ends M36

interpretation.statement: The appointment is bounded by its own column, which the application form caps at 36 months. No source ties that period to a work-package window, and the copy itself expects doctorates to outlast the funded period. A compliant 36-month appointment starting after month 1 outlasts a package ending at the project's own last month, so the rule fires on correct drafting.

evidence.quote: Where doctoral programmes extend beyond the funded period, institutions may provide complementary resources

adjudications.consequence: Nine out_of_window findings removed. The check now reports only non-overlap, the one relation the two windows share, and carries the overrun as a note with its months. The limit of that test is declared here: one month of overlap passes it. A stronger test would need a premise no source gives, and the obvious candidate is false - a 36-month appointment cannot cover a 36-month package unless it starts in month 1. Overlap is the strongest sound test available, and the appointment's end is noted rather than judged.
adjudications.operator_decision: The note stands for review on its own merits: nine candidates are employed to M40 while no work package runs past M36. Decide in R05 whether the work plan should state activity for months 37-40, or a project duration, or neither.
